Install the Julia packages used by latentmixtures

install_julia_packages.Rd

Installs LatentMixtures.jl (and optionally LatentClassCausal.jl, used by latentclasscausal) into the default Julia environment, either from local source directories (development mode, Pkg.develop) or from a Git URL (Pkg.add).

Usage

install_julia_packages(
  path = NULL,
  url = "https://github.com/williamlorder/LatentMixtures.jl",
  causal_path = NULL,
  causal_url = NULL,
  threads = NULL
)

Arguments

path

Local directory of LatentMixtures.jl, or NULL.

url

Git URL of LatentMixtures.jl, used when path is NULL (default: the package's GitHub repository).

causal_path

Optional local directory of LatentClassCausal.jl.

causal_url

Optional Git URL of LatentClassCausal.jl (used when causal_path is NULL), e.g. "https://github.com/williamlorder/LatentClassCausal.jl".

The GitHub repositories are private: Git must be able to authenticate to github.com (e.g. gh auth setup-git).

threads

Optional number of Julia threads (or "auto") for this R session; sets JULIA_NUM_THREADS before Julia starts and has no effect if Julia is already running.

Value

Invisibly TRUE. Called for its side effect on the Julia environment; errors from Julia's package manager are passed on.

Details

Julia (>= 1.12) must be installed, for example with juliaup, and found by JuliaConnectoR: set the environment variable JULIA_BINDIR (e.g. in ~/.Renviron) if julia is not on the PATH. This function starts Julia if needed; it does not load LatentMixtures.jl (that happens in lm_start()). Installation is needed once per Julia environment, not once per R session. For GPU estimation (device = "cuda"), install CUDA.jl into the same environment yourself.

See also

lm_start()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
install_julia_packages()      # from GitHub
install_julia_packages(causal_url = "https://github.com/williamlorder/LatentClassCausal.jl")
install_julia_packages(path = "~/src/LatentMixtures.jl",
                       causal_path = "~/src/LatentClassCausal.jl")
} # }
